title: Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve Board finalizes rules that tailor its regulations for domestic and foreign banks to more closely match their risk profiles
主要内容: The Federal Reserve Board finalized rules to tailor regulations for domestic and foreign banks, aligning them more closely with their risk profiles. The rules reduce compliance requirements for less risky firms while maintaining strict standards for larger, more complex banks. Banks with $100 billion or more in total assets are categorized into four groups based on factors like asset size, cross-jurisdictional activity, reliance on short-term wholesale funding, nonbank assets, and off-balance sheet exposure. The rules apply liquidity standards to a foreign bank's U.S. intermediate holding company (IHC) based on the IHC's risk profile, rather than the combined U.S. operations of the foreign bank. The Board estimates the changes will result in a 0.6 percent decrease in required capital and a 2 percent reduction in required liquid assets for banks with assets of $100 billion or more. The rules do not reduce capital or liquidity requirements for firms in the highest risk categories. The rules will take effect 60 days after publication in the Federal Register, with the comment period ending on January 9, 2020.
